small_guidance:
- Add larger-tile autotune configs targeting this square 16384×4096×4096 GEMM: BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4, and BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64. Also try BLOCK_K=128 stages=2 — K=4096 benefits from deeper pipelining with bigger K tiles.
- Drop the per-iteration K mask: K=4096 is divisible by all candidate BLOCK_K values, so replace masked loads with unconditional `tl.load` in the hot loop (use a separate tail iteration only if K%BLOCK_K!=0). This cuts predicate overhead in the inner loop.
- Use `evict_policy='evict_last'` on the A tile (reused across N tiles within a group) and `evict_first` on B, and ensure GROUP_M=8 — already set, but try GROUP_M=16 since M/BLOCK_M is 64-128.
large_guidance:
- Consider a split-K or stream-K persistent GEMM: with M=N=K=4096-ish, a persistent kernel with one CTA per SM iterating over output tiles will reduce launch/grid overhead and improve L2 reuse vs the current one-tile-per-program scheme.
- Switch input dtype handling: cast x and weight_t to fp16/bf16 inside the kernel (or store weight_t in bf16) and accumulate in fp32 with `tl.dot`. fp32×fp32 tf32 on a 4090 peaks far below fp16 tensor-core throughput; bf16 inputs would roughly 2× the FLOP/s ceiling while staying within 5e-2 tolerance.
- Fuse the epilogue more aggressively by writing directly through a 2D block pointer (`tl.make_block_ptr`) with boundary checks lifted out — this often gives a few % over manual masked stores at these tile sizes.
